solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Tradesman’s first to applaud as it’s put back into service (7)

indicatorNotes.first to: the first letter to 'applaud' is its opening A
indicatorNotes.put back: words put back run in the reverse direction
indicatorNotes.into: the reversed letters go into RN

blocks.note: the two words as they stand, reversed to TISA
RN = Royal Navy, the Senior Service

annotation.surface: A craftsman's work is clapped as a machine is returned to working order.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s on Tradesman is 'is', which then reads with 'put back into': AS IT is put back into RN. The Royal Navy is the Senior Service, so 'service' gives RN.
annotation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, a tradesman.

entries.clue: City like to restrict United, and can (6)

indicatorNotes.to restrict: AS restricts U by closing round it

blocks.note: as = like, as in 'dressed as a clown'
U = United, as in football team names

annotation.surface: A fan of a football club talks of hemming in United, with a drink can in hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Like' is the word AS, not a verb; U for United comes from team names like Man U.
annotation.definitionFit: Austin is the state capital of Texas.

entries.clue: Malign suggestion conveys a bit less than expected (7)

indicatorNotes.conveys: to convey is to carry, so TRACE carries DU inside it
indicatorNotes.a bit less than: DUE falls a bit short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: a trace is a slight suggestion, as in 'a trace of irony'
expected = DUE, cut short by one letter

annotation.surface: A snide hint implies that someone earned rather less than they were meant to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Malign' reads as an adjective with 'suggestion'; it is the verb, to speak ill of, which is what traduce means.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to speak falsely and damagingly of someone.

entries.clue: Handsome older man lives for high times (6,3)

indicatorNotes.high: high means intoxicated, so the letters of LIVES FOR are all over the place

blocks.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

annotation.surface: A dashing older man is said to live for the good life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High times' looks like a phrase for fun; 'high' is the anagram signal and 'times' is the X of multiplication.
annotation.definitionFit: A silver fox is an attractive grey-haired older man.

entries.clue: Yes, end war somehow, with a conclusion to hostility when resolutions come into effect? (3,5,3)

indicatorNotes.somehow: somehow says the letters come together in some unstated way
indicatorNotes.conclusion to: the conclusion to hostility is its final letter

blocks.note: A is used as is, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A peace treaty is signed, ending hostility, just as new resolutions take effect.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pretends the resolutions are diplomatic ones settling a war; the definition wants the promises people make on 1 January.
annotation.definitionFit: New Year resolutions are meant to start on 1 January; the question mark flags the playful definition.

entries.clue: County embraces introduction of treatment with universal medication (7)

indicatorNotes.embraces: LINCS embraces, or holds, the two letters
indicatorNotes.introduction of: the introduction of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Lincs is the short form of Lincolnshire, an English county
U = universal, the film classification for all ages

annotation.surface: A county council starts a treatment programme with medicine for everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: Lincs, short for Lincolnshire, is an English county. Here 'with' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Linctus is a syrupy cough medicine.

entries.clue: Violent robbery topped former convict (3)

indicatorNotes.topped: a topped word loses its head, the first letter in a down clue

blocks.note: BLAG, slang for a violent robbery, loses its B

annotation.surface: A former prisoner was involved in a violent raid.
annotation.walkthrough: Blag is British criminal slang for a robbery with violence; an old lag is a habitual or former convict.
annotation.definitionFit: A lag, usually 'old lag', is British slang for a former prisoner.

entries.clue: Stylish tailcoat — nothing on the inside, no pockets (5)

indicatorNotes.nothing on the inside: with nothing inside, tailcoat keeps only its outer letters
indicatorNotes.pockets: to pocket is to put in, so NAY holds TT

blocks.note: TAILCOAT emptied leaves its outer letters T…T

annotation.surface: A tailor describes a smart tailcoat cut without any pockets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No pockets' reads as a feature of the coat, but 'no' is a letter source and 'pockets' the instruction to put something inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Natty means smart and stylish in dress.

entries.clue: Port is comparatively piquant (7)

blocks.note: a port city on the Moroccan side of the Strait of Gibraltar

annotation.surface: A wine note: port is sharper in taste than the others.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port' reads as the fortified wine, which fits 'piquant'; it is the Moroccan city of Tangier, and 'comparatively' asks for the -ER form of tangy.
annotation.definitionFit: Tangier is a port on the Strait of Gibraltar, and tangier is the comparative of tangy.

entries.clue: Husband unhappy with friends turning up last-minute (8)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

annotation.surface: A husband is miserable because his friends arrive at the last moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' looks like friends arriving; it is the reversal of the whole string H SAD PALS.
annotation.definitionFit: Last-minute work is rushed and careless, which is slapdash.

entries.clue: Rogue Conservative friend invested in stolen goods (9)

indicatorNotes.invested in: to be invested in is to be put inside, so C and ALLY go into SWAG

annotation.surface: A crooked Tory politician's pal has put money into stolen property.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invested in' reads as a money term; here it only means placed inside SWAG.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both playful words for a mischievous rascal rather than a real villain.

entries.clue: Country’s head of agriculture got back around noon (5)

indicatorNotes.head of: the head of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.back: GOT back reads it from right to left
indicatorNotes.around: the reversed GOT goes around N

blocks.note: the word as it stands, reversed to TOG
N = noon, the abbreviation used in times

annotation.surface: A nation's farming minister returned home at midday.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'has', joining the definition: TOG around N, and the head of agriculture's A follows it.
annotation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom in the South Pacific.

entries.clue: One sister has run away to get engaged (2,3)

indicatorNotes.has run away: R, for run, has gone from NURSE

blocks.note: a sister is a senior nurse in a British hospital
R = run in cricket scoring; this letter leaves NURSE

annotation.surface: A nun or sibling elopes in order to marry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run away to get engaged' is an elopement; 'engaged' means busy, as a phone line or toilet is. In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse.
annotation.definitionFit: Engaged here is the busy sense used of a phone line or a toilet door, not betrothed.

entries.clue: One arrives in good time — European travelling by rail and road (5,4)

indicatorNotes.travelling: travelling letters move about into a new order

annotation.surface: A European commuter who goes by train and car always turns up on time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Road' shrinks to its abbreviation RD before joining BY RAIL in the anagram; 'and' just adds it.
annotation.definitionFit: From the proverb 'the early bird catches the worm': the phrase names anyone who turns up ahead of time.

entries.clue: Ignoring temperature, desperate to support engineers — I’m compensating (11)

indicatorNotes.Ignoring: BURSTING ignores T, leaving it out
indicatorNotes.to support: in a down clue, a supporting word sits below, so RE comes on top

blocks.note: bursting = desperate, as in 'bursting to tell'
T = temperature; this letter leaves BURSTING

annotation.surface: An engineer, eager to help but ignoring the heat, is paying people back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I'm' sits at the end of the clue, looking attached to the definition, but it is wordplay. RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; 'desperate' is bursting, as in bursting to go.
annotation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to compensate someone for money spent.

entries.clue: Things such as drama roles encapsulating revolutionary from Niger (10,4)

indicatorNotes.encapsulating: PARTS encapsulates, or encloses, the jumbled letters
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: revolutionary letters turn over into a new order

blocks.note: parts are roles in a play

annotation.surface: Acting parts are given to a rebel from the African country of Niger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary from Niger' reads as a rebel; 'revolutionary' is the anagram signal and 'from Niger' its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: drama is one of the arts presented on stage, alongside dance and music.

entries.clue: Ultimately, crushing defeat ended in whitewash (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Ultimately: ultimately points to the final letter

annotation.surface: A crushing defeat finished with the team losing without scoring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whitewash' is a sports term for a total rout, which fits the surface; the definition wants its sense of covering up faults.
annotation.definitionFit: Whitewash in its figurative sense is covering up faults, the same idiom as passing over them lightly.

entries.clue: Observe fewer things without flaws (8)

blocks.note: less = fewer, of a quantity of things

annotation.surface: An inspector notices fewer items that are without defects.
annotation.walkthrough: The split falls after 'things': 'without flaws' is the definition, not 'things without flaws'.
annotation.definitionFit: Spotless means perfectly clean, without a flaw.

entries.clue: On bed, I explored being kinky — she’s very fair (8,6)

indicatorNotes.being kinky: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

annotation.surface: A woman confesses to some bedroom experimentation, and her partner is very pale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as just, of a lover; here it is hair colour. A peroxide blonde's hair is bleached with hydrogen peroxide.
annotation.definitionFit: The fairness is hair colour: hydrogen peroxide bleaches hair to a very pale shade.

entries.clue: Unrestrained tirade about a person occupying seat (7)

indicatorNotes.about: RANT goes about, or around, the other letters

blocks.note: an MP holds a seat in Parliament

annotation.surface: Someone launches into an uncontrolled tirade about a fellow passenger taking a seat.
annotation.walkthrough: The seat is a parliamentary one, so the person occupying it is an MP.
annotation.definitionFit: Rampant means unrestrained, flourishing unchecked.

entries.clue: Operating during the day, vessel is brought in by radio control (7)

blocks.note: the dial is the tuning control on a radio

annotation.surface: A ship working by daylight is guided into port by radio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' reads as a ship being brought into harbour; it is an URN, and the radio control is a tuning DIAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A zoologist's term, from Latin diurnus, daily; its opposite is nocturnal.

entries.clue: Climber eating hard, out-of-date bread (6)

indicatorNotes.eating: PEA eats SET, taking it inside

blocks.note: the pea plant climbs with tendrils
set = hardened, as of jelly or concrete

annotation.surface: A mountaineer is chewing on hard, stale bread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, and 'out-of-date' means withdrawn currency, not stale food.
annotation.definitionFit: The peseta was Spain's currency until the euro replaced it; bread is slang for money.

entries.clue: Literary character’s motto central to storyline in book, right? (3,6)

indicatorNotes.central to: the letter central to storyline is its middle one
indicatorNotes.in: in places SAW and Y inside TOME, splitting the book open

blocks.note: a tome is a large book
a saw is a proverb or saying

annotation.surface: A reader asks whether a character's catchphrase sums up the plot of the novel.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is', linking the definition; 'motto' is an old SAW, not a slogan. Storyline has nine letters, so its fifth, Y, is central.
annotation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is the boy hero of Mark Twain's novel.

entries.clue: A third of biscuit, absorbed by beverage, is lost (2,3)

indicatorNotes.third of: the third of biscuit means its third letter, S, not a fraction of it
indicatorNotes.absorbed by: TEA absorbs S, soaking it up inside

annotation.surface: A soggy biscuit, dunked in tea, falls apart and disappears into the cup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A third of' looks like a fraction; A is the first letter of the answer and 'third of biscuit' is its third letter, S.
annotation.definitionFit: A ship out of sight of land has no bearings, so the idiom extends to anyone bewildered.

entries.clue: Sea foam close to outcrop, birds circling around (5)

indicatorNotes.close to: the letter close to the end of outcrop is its last
indicatorNotes.circling: the birds circle P, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.around: around turns EMUS back to front

blocks.note: emus are birds, reversed to SUME

annotation.surface: Foam gathers by a rocky outcrop as seabirds wheel overhead.
annotation.walkthrough: The seabirds of the surface are EMUS, flightless birds that could hardly circle anything.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary word from Latin spuma, foam, used of the froth whipped off waves.

entries.clue: Non-commissioned officer cut back tests (5)

indicatorNotes.back: back reads SM AXE from right to left

annotation.surface: A sergeant was reduced in rank after failing tests.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut back' reads as one phrase meaning reduced; 'cut' is AXE and 'back' reverses the whole of SM AXE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: school or university examinations are formal tests.

entries.clue: Welshman tucked into good food — beef (9)

indicatorNotes.tucked into: EVAN is tucked into RICE, placed inside it

blocks.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name

annotation.surface: A Welshman eagerly tucks into a good meal of beef.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beef' is on the menu in the surface; it is also slang for a complaint. 'Tucked into' is eating in the surface and insertion in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Beef is informal slang for a complaint, as in 'what's your beef?'.

entries.clue: My hotel’s out of butter (3)

indicatorNotes.’s out of: H is out of GHEE, removed from it

blocks.note: ghee is clarified butter used in South Asian cooking
H = hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet; this letter leaves GHEE

annotation.surface: A guest complains that their hotel has run out of butter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive; it is the exclamation 'My!', which GEE also is.
annotation.definitionFit: Gee and my are both mild exclamations of surprise.

entries.clue: Model had to accept university place (7)

indicatorNotes.to accept: SIT and ATE together accept U between them

blocks.note: to sit for a portrait is to model

annotation.surface: A model had to take a place at university.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had' reads as 'was obliged'; it is ATE, as in having a meal. 'Place' is the verb, to put somewhere.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to put something in a particular position.

entries.clue: Pass artist cuddling sick animal (7)

indicatorNotes.cuddling: RA cuddles ILL, wrapping around it

blocks.note: to go is to pass, as a turn in a game

annotation.surface: A painter hugs a poorly pet as it passes away.
annotation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the standard artist; 'Pass' is GO, your turn.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the largest of the great apes is simply an animal.
